groups.description: In these examples, the text judges a reduced or approximate result adequate locally: information loss is called negligible, visual inspection is treated as sufficient assurance in a particular estimation case, and an approximate brightness-to-lumen relationship is considered sufficient for the project. The judgements are reported, not independently validated.
groups.label: Local sufficiency judgements despite loss or approximation
groups.rationale: The higher-level inference is that these different evaluations share an operation of declaring local sufficiency rather than demanding maximal exactness. This is a bounded review candidate for how adequacy is expressed, not a stable trait. Such judgements are common in technical explanation, and the observations neither establish distinctiveness nor justify transferring one case's confidence to another.
variation_notes: A01::O0010 describes a reduced-basis reconstruction and calls the lost information negligible; it does not make a claim about statistical testing.

A03::O0012 acknowledges that a robustness test would finish the work but treats visual inspection as providing the necessary assurance in the specific municipal case, with a stated margin of confidence.
A09::O0006 explicitly notes that LEDs are not perfectly linear and ties the adequacy of the approximation to this project's purpose.

groups.description: Two explanations explicitly restrict the reach of a technical claim: power-law behaviour is described as usually applying only over portions of a quantity's measurements, and the illustrated quantum measurement behaviour is said not to apply to all quantities.
groups.label: Explicit limits on generalizing a technical claim
groups.rationale: Both observations directly qualify a possible universal reading by identifying a restricted domain or exceptions. This is a bounded candidate for reviewing how generalization is limited in explanations. These are conventional scientific caveats, so their recurrence alone establishes neither distinctiveness nor a stable author trait, and the underlying claims have not been independently checked.
variation_notes: A03::O0004 limits the power law to regions of the measurements and states that other regions follow different laws.
A04::O0010 identifies pairs of quantum quantities that can be measured together and yield a well-defined truth table, rather than describing a numerical range of validity.

groups.description: The two observations limit software or standard-adoption claims to the time of writing: YAML-only configuration of a REST sensor is qualified by 'ad oggi', and the assertion about llms.txt adoption is qualified by 'al momento in cui scrivo'. Neither observation establishes the present state of those technologies.
groups.label: Time-indexed claims about changing technology
groups.rationale: Both claims explicitly carry a temporal qualification rather than being presented as timeless facts. This is a bounded review candidate for time-indexing changeable technical claims. Such qualifications are common in software writing, and these instances alone do not demonstrate distinctiveness, a general habit, or correctness of the underlying statements.
variation_notes: A10::O0005 qualifies a configuration constraint affecting the REST sensor.
A11::O0005 qualifies the stated adoption of an immature standard, including the assertion that only OpenAI uses it at the time of writing.

groups.description: The observations connect practical guidance to first-person experience: time spent discovering an API parameter requirement, and a project-specific shell-history solution described as the most practical one found. They do not provide comparative benchmarks or establish that the advice works in every setting.
groups.label: First-person experience as local support for practical guidance
groups.rationale: The inferential step is reading these first-person accounts as local experiential support for the accompanying practical guidance. This is a candidate for review, not a personality or identity claim. Experience-based advice is commonplace, and a troubleshooting account and a preference among solutions provide different kinds of support rather than a uniform testing method.
variation_notes: A11::O0006 reports two hours spent understanding the need to request four PageSpeed Insights API categories explicitly, and frames the warning as sparing readers that difficulty.
A12::O0004 endorses separating shell history by project as the most practical solution the writer has found; the projection supplies no systematic comparison of alternatives.

groups.description: These observations explicitly qualify the precision of a treatment: an explanation disclaims exam-level rigour, a representation is approximate because equations have not been solved, and an interpolation is described as a linear simplification. They do not establish a common error bound or validation method.
groups.label: Declared limits of rigour or approximation
groups.rationale: The inferential step is grouping a pedagogical scope disclaimer with computational and modelling approximations as qualifications of the treatment's precision. This is a thematic grouping of different limitations, not evidence of a distinctive author practice or a recurring editorial structure.
variation_notes: A01::O0002 limits the intended rigour of the exposition; it does not identify a particular numerical approximation.
A07::O0010 attributes the approximate view to not having solved the equations.
A09::O0004 qualifies the transition between two model regimes as a linear simplification; the projection supplies no error estimate.

groups.description: The observations identify different obstacles to representing or using information: an overly schematic community model, loss of distinct measurements through binning, visualization difficulties at higher system order, and missing building-height data for an occlusion model. No common assessment metric is supplied.
groups.label: Named constraints on representation and practical use
groups.rationale: This is a thematic synthesis, not an author-pattern claim. The inferential step is treating model fidelity, measurement distinctness, display feasibility, and missing attributes as representational constraints. Their causes and consequences remain different; the grouping does not imply a shared validation procedure or equivalent severity.
variation_notes: A02::O0008 concerns the hierarchical model's inability to represent interpersonal relationships adequately because it is too schematic.
A03::O0005 concerns aggregation: after binning, measurements are no longer available as distinct entities.
A07::O0011 concerns visualization becoming complex and ineffective, potentially impossible, as the system's order increases; it does not claim that the underlying measurements are lost.
A09::O0011 connects the frequent absence of OSM building-height data to limited practical usefulness of an occlusion model, despite commonly available planimetric data.

groups.description: The treatments explicitly assume a physical setup or property: preparation in the up state for the logical-OR experiment, and constant mass for the mechanics discussion. These are local premises, not empirical findings about every system.
groups.label: Explicit physical premises for a worked treatment
groups.rationale: Both observations directly state assumptions used in their respective treatments. They are grouped thematically as conventional modelling premises; the evidence does not support a distinctive assumption-setting style or a recurring presentation format.
variation_notes: A04::O0005 specifies an initial preparation of the quantum system for the experiment being described.
A06::O0007 assumes constant mass and additionally describes that condition as holding in the great majority of cases; that prevalence claim is reported without independent verification.

groups.description: The observations give mathematical formalism a role in discussing quantum mechanics: one asks readers to rely on mathematics rather than intuitive understanding, while another motivates a formulation by its exposure of an algebraic formalism used in quantum theory.
groups.label: Mathematical formalism in explanations of quantum mechanics
groups.rationale: The inferential step is connecting an explicit preference for mathematical reasoning over intuition with a statement about the relevance of an algebraic framework. The grouping concerns the subject matter and its stated mathematical basis; it does not establish a general author preference, prove that intuition is always inadequate, or verify the physics.
variation_notes: A05::O0002 makes a direct methodological recommendation about reasoning at quantum scales.
A06::O0003 explains the quantum relevance of the algebraic formalism of kinematics and dynamics through the Hamiltonian formulation; it does not itself contrast that formalism with intuition.

groups.description: Both observations state that, with a force specified, initial conditions identify a unique solution of Newton's equation. The recurrence is of a mechanics claim within the stated setups, not evidence of independently established uniqueness for arbitrary force laws.
groups.label: Initial conditions as grounds for unique Newtonian evolution
groups.rationale: The observations repeat a specific content-level connection between initial conditions and uniqueness of motion. A thematic classification preserves that connection without turning a standard mechanics explanation into an author characteristic. The projections are insufficient for assessing all mathematical conditions needed for the claims.
variation_notes: A06::O0004 invokes the principle of determinism and states that each solution is uniquely identified by initial conditions for an assigned force.
A07::O0004 specifies a force written as F(x, v, t), an initial time and phase-space point, and states that exactly one solution determines the subsequent evolution in the case considered.

groups.description: Within the unit explanation, dimensional reduction is used to justify an energy unit divided by squared speed as a mass unit, and mass-energy equivalence is invoked to explain the choice of the speed of light. These are distinct warrants for related parts of the explanation.
groups.label: Two formal warrants for the mass unit eV/c²
groups.rationale: The observations form a tightly local thematic group about the justification of a unit. Dimensional compatibility and the physical reason for choosing c are complementary, not interchangeable arguments. Their use in one explanation does not establish a cross-topic author pattern or independently verify the derivation.
variation_notes: A08::O0006 reasons from the dimensional expression reducing to mass to support the unit eV/c².
A08::O0007 answers why c is selected by recalling E = mc² and its relation between rest mass and energy.

unclustered_observations.reason: This makes a specific connection between an eigenvalue's relative magnitude and informational contribution. No other projected observation supplies the same evaluative indicator; grouping it solely under mathematical justification would obscure its local content.

The criticism of an associated experiment's rigour is not accompanied here by an assessment method. It differs from limiting the rigour of an exposition, and no second observation supports the same critique of an experimental basis.

This explicitly identifies an unresolved research question about the triangle's role in social communities. No second projection identifies a comparable open question; combining it with model limitations would blur research uncertainty and representational inadequacy.

This prescribes a hypothesis test for estimator robustness. No second observation independently prescribes the same validation operation; the separate observation about visual assurance records a case-specific relaxation rather than another instance of the prescription.

The 25% false probability for B OR A, contrasted with certainty for A OR B, is a local result of the described experiment. There is no second comparable quantified uncertainty statement to support a group.

This asserts that the quantum character of reality is established. The other quantum projections concern formalism or the limits of particular examples, not a recurring form of asserting demonstrated certainty; no independent verification is available.

The zero derivative of energy is justified specifically by restricting attention to solutions of Newton's equation. This does not repeat the uniqueness claim or the unit-choice warrants, so those groups would conflate different inferential operations.

This cautiously proposes usefulness for particular dashboard audiences. No second projection offers the same audience-directed utility assessment; a personal preference among shell-history solutions supplies a different basis and object of judgement.

This attributes crawler criteria to a named external source. No second projected observation records comparable source attribution, and mathematical warrants or first-person experience are not equivalent support practices.

This offers a probabilistic assumption about a user's development and git context. It is distinct from fixed physical premises and from a potential usefulness claim, and there is no second comparable inference about user circumstances.
